item.title: How Might the Trump-Xi Summit Impact U.S. Farmers?
item.description: The U.S. agricultural industry has borne the brunt of the recent U.S.-China trade conflict. Now, farmers watch closely as Presidents Trump and Xi seek a potential agreement in Beijing, but longer-term structural trends make a quick fix unlikely.

item.title: A U.S. Campaign to Exploit Beijing’s Weaknesses
item.description: The Chinese Communist Party has systemic weaknesses. U.S. operations should capitalize on them.

item.title: States Weekly: May 13, 2026
item.description: This edition of States Weekly covers May 13, 2026.

item.title: America Has Lost Its Leverage Over China
item.description: The Trump-Xi summit will reinforce a new set of implicit rules and assumptions for managing relations that ultimately favor China, argues Henrietta Levin in Foreign Policy.

item.title: Is the United States Prepared for a War with China?
item.description: Despite recent progress, the U.S. military would face serious challenges fighting a protracted war with China because of a lack of long-range munitions, air defense systems, and unmanned systems, along with vulnerable bases and critical infrastructure in the Indo-Pacific.

item.title: The U.S.-China Trade Truce Has Not Solved the Gallium Problem
item.description: The upcoming Trump-Xi summit offers an opportunity to press Beijing on its commitments on critical minerals.

item.title: A Confident Beijing Welcomes President Trump
item.description: Scott Kennedy lays out how China’s leaders are approaching the upcoming Trump-Xi summit, and why China feels remarkably more confident compared to the first such summit in 2017.

item.title: China’s Nuclear Energy Priorities Under Its 15th Five-Year Plan
item.description: China's 15th Five-Year Plan has far-ranging implications for the nuclear energy, not only for the future of global nuclear sector but also for China’s influence and competitiveness in innovation and supply chains.

item.title: What May 15 Means for Somalia’s Federal Architecture and Global Shipping
item.description: New reports of piracy off Somalia’s coast are grabbing headlines, but the bigger story is a looming constitutional crisis on May 15 that poses a long-term risk to the country’s federal legitimacy, regional stability, and, ultimately, to global shipping lanes.
